claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The splashdown occurred at 0007 GMT on April 11.
The Artemis II crew included Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew concluded a 10-day mission.
Artemis II marked the first human return from the Moon since 1972.
The landing occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The landing location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
The Artemis II mission duration was 10 days.
The Orion spacecraft separated from the service module at 7:33 p.m. EDT.
The Orion spacecraft separated from the service module to prepare for atmospheric reentry.
The Orion spacecraft endured temperatures of ~3,000°F.
The crew was extracted by NASA and U.S. Navy teams following splashdown
